newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady after RBI intervention.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady after RBI intervention.

text.p: Dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) led the the rupee to close at 35.85/86 on Monday, down from the opening 35.84/85, dealers said.
The RBI purchased in lots of $5.0 million, they said.
The rupee moved in a narrow groove of 35.847/865. The dollar saw a day's high of 35.860 on Monday.
"There is nothing to excite the spot rupee market as it hugs the 35.85 area so snugly," said a foreign bank in a commentary.
The bank saw some chance of revived dollar demand before the month-end. But a dealer at another bank said he did not see any sign of major dollar demand until February 15.

The second tranche of redemption of India Development Bonds comes up on February 15. Some dealers expect that payment in foreign exchange on these bonds to expatriate Indians could be as high as $1.0 billion.
The forward dollar premia opened lower and fell further, dealers said. July dollar closed at 1.29/1.32 rupees compared to the opening level of 1.31/1.34 rupees, they said.
The six-month annualised premium ended Monday at 7.14 percent, down from the weekend closing of 7.37 percent.
